{"path":"neuron_growth_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW single self-contained HTML file: an animated neon "neuron growth" simulation using HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript and dat.gui (the ONLY allowed external library, loaded via CDN script tag: https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/dat-gui/0.7.9/dat.gui.min.js). No other external libraries, frameworks, modules, images, or assets. Do not mention any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style anywhere in code or comments.

PAGE / LAYOUT:
- Dark page background #05070f. One 800x800 <canvas> centered horizontally and vertically (flexbox on body, margin 0, min-height 100vh). Canvas has a subtle outer glow via CSS box-shadow using #101a3a and a thin 1px border rgba(0,229,255,0.25).
- Small caption/title text under or above canvas in #ffd400, monospace, subtle letter-spacing (e.g. "NEURAL GROWTH SIMULATION").

EXACT NEON PALETTE (use as defaults):
- Background: #05070f, Background glow: #101a3a, Main branch: #00e5ff, Secondary branch accent: #d6ff00, Synapse: #ff2bd6, Pulse: #fff36a, UI/accent: #ffd400, grid/scanline: rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08).

SIMULATION (vanilla JS, lightweight arrays/objects only):
- Setup: generate `neuronCount` (default 5, range 3-6 typical) seed neurons at random positions near the canvas center (within ~120px radius of center). Each seed has x, y, and an array of branches.
- Branch growth: recursive branching structure. Each branch: start point, current tip point, angle, depth, thickness (random 0.6-2.2, thinner at higher depth), remaining length, color flag (main vs accent ~15% accent), array of sampled points (for drawing smooth quadratic curves), alive flag. Growth is ANIMATED step-by-step: each frame every growing branch advances its tip by `growthSpeed` pixels, appends points, angle wanders by small random amounts scaled by `curvature` (smooth organic curves). When a branch's remaining length is exhausted and depth < maxDepth, it spawns 1-2 child branches (second child only if Math.random() < splitChance); occasionally (small chance) a growing branch also spawns a smaller side branch mid-growth. Hard cap total branches (e.g. 900) and stop growth when cap reached or no branches alive — network then considered stable.
- Drawing branches: render each branch's points as a smooth path using quadraticCurveTo (midpoint technique), strokeStyle branch or accent color, lineWidth = thickness, shadowBlur ~8-12 with shadowColor same as stroke for neon glow.
- Synapse detection: periodically (every few frames, not every frame) check growing/finished branch TIPS against tips of branches belonging to OTHER neurons; if distance < synapseDistance and no existing synapse between that pair (store a Set of "idA-idB" keys to prevent duplicates), create a synapse {x, y (midpoint), a, b, phase}. Cap synapse count (e.g. 120).
- Pulses: after (and during) growth, spawn pulses at random synapses at a rate controlled by pulseFrequency (probability per frame). A pulse travels from neuron a's seed position toward the synapse point and on to neuron b's seed position (simple two-segment interpolation, t from 0..1 advanced by pulseSpeed). Draw as a bright spark: small circle with large shadowBlur in pulse color, brightness scaled by pulseBrightness, plus a short fading trail (2-3 previous positions). Synapses glow softly: drawn as small circles in synapse color with shadowBlur scaled by synapseGlow, alpha pulsing over time via sin(time + phase).

RENDERING (requestAnimationFrame loop):
- Each frame: fill canvas with background color at low alpha (e.g. 0.18-0.3) for slight motion trails; optionally draw a faint background radial glow (#101a3a) and a sparse dark grid in rgba(0,229,255,0.08) every 40px.
- Draw order: grid/glow -> branches -> synapses -> pulses -> vignette -> scanlines.
- Vignette: radial gradient from transparent center to rgba(0,0,0,0.55) at edges, drawn each frame.
- Scanlines: subtle horizontal lines every 3-4px using rgba(0,229,255,0.08) at very low alpha, or pre-rendered once to an offscreen canvas pattern drawn with low alpha; keep it cheap. Optional faint animated noise: a few dozen random 1px dots per frame at very low alpha.
- Keep everything lightweight: no particle systems, no physics, no pathfinding.

GUI (dat.gui), folders exactly: Growth, Synapses, Pulses, Visuals.
- Growth: neuron count (1-10 step 1), branch growth speed (0.5-6), max branch depth (1-8 step 1), branch split chance (0-1), branch curvature (0-1), max branch length (20-200). Changing these (except speed) regenerates the network (onFinishChange -> regenerate).
- Synapses: synapse distance threshold (5-80), synapse glow strength (0-30).
- Pulses: pulse speed (0.5-8), pulse frequency (0-0.2), pulse brightness (0-2).
- Visuals: color pickers for background color, branch color, accent branch color, synapse color, pulse color (defaults from palette above). Background color change takes effect immediately (clear canvas fully on change).
- Buttons (top level of GUI, not in folders): "regenerate network", "clear canvas", "pause / resume" (toggles animation loop; button name or label reflects state if easy).

CODE STRUCTURE: single <script> at end of body, compact and readable, with short comments marking sections: // --- Setup ---, // --- GUI setup ---, // --- Neuron growth ---, // --- Synapse detection ---, // --- Pulse animation ---, // --- Rendering ---. Use a single `params` object holding all GUI-bound values. Functions: initGUI(), regenerate(), clearCanvas(), growStep(), detectSynapses(), spawnPulse(), updatePulses(), render(), animate(). Pause flag skips update+render but keeps rAF alive (or stops/starts rAF — either fine)."}
